label: Heavy going
summary: A day held by two crises. In the Himalayas the 26 August glacial collapse passed a grim mark: Nepal and China confirmed more than 1,000 dead, with 3,916 still missing and some 900 hydropower workers unaccounted for. In the Gulf, a month of quiet ended — US forces struck launchers on Iran's Larak Island, Tehran fired on bases in Jordan and the UAE, a supertanker burned after hitting mines in Hormuz, and Brent topped $91. Flash floods killed two in the Grand Canyon; Congo's Ebola epidemic passed 5,700 cases. Against that, Libya's rival factions signed a UN-backed deal to hold elections within two years, EU defence ministers met in Ireland on drones and Patriots for Ukraine, Lebanon abolished the death penalty, and London surgeons removed a tumour under live AI guidance, saving a man's sight. No editorial adjustment.
